To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified SakA and MkpC interacting proteins in A. fumiguatus.
A. fumilgatus MpkC interacts with the cell wall integrity pathway components PtcB, MpkA, and PakA, as well as with SakA, in response to cell wall stress and osmotic stress.

we have identified the protein interactors of A. fumilgatus MAPKs SakA and MkpC, and that these interactors include proteins involved in the regulation of the response of the cell to osmotic and cell walls stresses, oxidative stress, and drug resistance.

a fundamental understanding of the role of SakA and its interactome in A. fumilagatus physiology and pathogenesis.
the characterization of protein interactions involved in the SakA/MkpC MAPK pathway of A. fumiga tus.
the identification of SakA and Mpck interactors under different stresses and the analysis of their biological roles.

the SakA and MpcK interactomes are composed by proteins involved in cell wall stress response, oxidative stress response, and cell cycle regulation.
SakA and its interactors play a role in the regulation of cell wall stress, osmotic stress and drug resistance.
SakA and MPKC interact with a wide range of proteins in A.fumigatus under osmotic and cell stress, and that these interactions are important for cell survival under stress conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a set of proteins that physically interact with the A. fumifatus MAPKs SakA and MkpC.
we describe the first protein interactomes for SakA and MkpC and the identification of a novel protein PakA as an important component of SakA/MkpC signaling pathway.
we describe the protein interactions of SakA and MpKC under osmotic and cell stress in the opportunistic human pathogen Aspergillus. fumigates.
